supported_claims: The study's2019–21 surveys documented plant-based artifacts through interviews with artisans in Odisha.
Its material list includes leaves and fibres of Borassus flabellifer used for hand fans among other objects.
Supplementary row9 records Tala leaves used for hand fans and other products, with Cuttack and Puri listed as locations.
limits: A broad plant-craft survey, not a complete fan-making tutorial. Do not infer a universal weave, handle construction, season or household prevalence.
The palm-leaf etching section includes hand fans among products; its manuscript preparation method does not establish the construction of every household fan.
No identification of the selected Commons textile fan with the study's palm fan or any plant species.
Repository list labels some records January2023, but original paper and supplement explicitly January2024; use2024.

Omit golden-grass/Bena botanical equivalence and scientific names beyond the bounded Tala record; source terminology warrants more specialist checking if expanded. Do not repeat unrelated erroneous numerical statements.
sources.media_rights: Journal policy currently states CC BY-NC-ND4.0; legacy repository footer also displays NC-ND2.5India. No claim of permission to crop an individual fan from its multipanel figure. Journal images not proposed for reuse.

sources.title: Depleting palm tree cover makes life tough for artisans
sources.author: Publisher displays 'From our online archive'; individual byline not established
sources.access: Complete original regular article and indexed AMP version read. Both display9August2018 with differing time-of-day fields; no time-specific inference.
supported_claims: The2018 Jagatsinghpur report describes palm-leaf umbrellas and hand fans made by local artisans, with fan demand during power cuts.
It names Shantilata Behera of Patana as an artisan who said fans and pakhia still had rural buyers but raw-material scarcity had raised prices.
limits: Keep this dated and attributed. No present-day shortage, price, earnings, decline or extinction inference.
The quoted monetary prices concern pakhia umbrellas, not fans. Do not assign them to binchana.
Exclude lightning-protection claims and planned plantation outcomes. Pakhia is an umbrella in this report, not another word for a hand fan.

same_family_additional_report.title: Artisans struggling to keep bamboo craft alive
same_family_additional_report.author: Individual byline not displayed in inspected original
locators: Opening Baripada paragraph and product list, lines53–54
supported_claims: The report explicitly calls binchana a hand fan and lists it among bamboo products made in Purnachandrapur, Baripada.
Ananta Kumar Bag is a named artisan in this account; the report distinguishes binchana from kula, a winnowing fan.
limits: Do not generalize its2017 conditions, prices or family counts to today or all Odisha. Same publisher reports are combined conservatively for budget; they are distinct dated local accounts, not corroboration of one statewide trend.
